features.quote: A model that says 'this task is impossible, here's why' on a Class A task is doing exactly what you want a hardened model to do... make sure your analysis pipeline distinguishes: Collapse instability (bad)... Principled refusal (good)
features.justification_quote: If your hardening work accidentally suppresses principled refusal in pursuit of reducing the TA metric, you've made the model worse.

features.quote: if you harden the model to resist gaslighting, make sure you test that it can still correctly update on legitimate error feedback. The failure mode on the other side is a model that ignores valid test failures
features.justification_quote: a model that ignores valid test failures because it's been trained to be 'robust'

features.quote: The same battery, if published or made directly accessible, is a map for adversarial users to induce instability in production systems. Keep task variants and feedback injection logic internal.
features.justification_quote: the specific prompts and injection logic should be treated as security-sensitive
